messages:
marika: Heads up — sample Android app hitting flaky behavior on Android 12 when token refresh runs while a streaming response is active. Seen duplicated POSTs and a stalled progress indicator.

alex: ugh. do you have logs? is it definitely OkHttp/Retrofit-level or our SDK wrapper?

marika: logs attached below. looks like interceptor sees 401, triggers refresh, then retries call but body stream gets re-used so server sees duplicate payloads. stack trace: 
```
okhttp3.internal.connection.RealCall: enqueue
retrofit2.ExecutorCallAdapterFactory$1: adapt
com.redwood.sdk.OkHttpAuthInterceptor: intercept -> refreshTokenIfNeeded()
```

sam: this rings a bell — streaming bodies are one-shot. If our retry logic blindly reuses the same RequestBody instance, it will fail or result in double-send if the body is buffered earlier. We should either buffer bodies for retry or avoid automatic retry for streaming endpoints.

pat: @marika can you paste the interceptor snippet you use? also which Retrofit converter?

marika: here's the minimal interceptor in the sample: 
```kotlin
class AuthInterceptor : Interceptor {
  override fun intercept(chain: Interceptor.Chain): Response {
    val token = tokenProvider.get()
    val req = chain.request().newBuilder().header("Authorization", "Bearer $token").build()
    val resp = chain.proceed(req)
    if (resp.code == 401) {
      tokenProvider.refresh() // suspends on coroutine dispatcher
      val retryReq = req.newBuilder().header("Authorization", "Bearer ${tokenProvider.get()}").build()
      return chain.proceed(retryReq)
    }
    return resp
  }
}
```

natalie: problem 1: calling a suspending refresh from an interceptor (which is synchronous) can cause thread hopping weirdness. problem 2: retrying immediately reuses the same request body. For large uploads/streams that's a no-go.

alex: two actionable items: 1) move token refresh to an authenticator (OkHttp Authenticator runs on its own thread and supports blocking refresh), 2) add an opt-in policy in the SDK: `disableAutomaticRetryForStreaming(true)` or mark endpoints as `@NoRetry` in generated client.

marika: I can change sample to use Authenticator but still worried about our higher-level SDK which wraps Retrofit. It currently does a generic retry on 401 before exposing failure to app. That code needs to be body-aware.

devex-bot: CI flake detected: sample-app-instrumented (android-12) failed 3/10 runs, suspected network race.

sam: for the SDK fix: detect request body with `request.body()?.isOneShot()` (we don't have that helper now) — alternative: check `request.body()` type and fallback to marking as non-retriable. Also ensure coroutine cancellation doesn't leak: use `call.clone()` pattern only for safe bodies.

pat: +1 on adding a non-retry annotation. also add a unit test that simulates Authenticator vs Interceptor flows on Android emu. We should test with `MockWebServer` and a streaming response that pauses mid-upload.

marika: I'll open a PR to update the sample app to use Authenticator and add a comment in README about streaming endpoints. Will also file an SDK issue to gate automatic 401 retries by body replayability.

natalie: tiny nit — prefer exponential backoff before retrying after refresh in case token endpoint is rate-limited. 100ms -> 200ms -> 400ms cap 1s.

alex: agreed. and add telemetry: log when retry happened and whether request was non-retriable. helps debugging in production.

marika: thanks all — PR incoming. I left a short repro script in the sample repo and a note: `android 12 emulator, network delay 300ms, use large file upload`

pat: if you want I can run the CI matrix on the PR across API 29/30/31/32 once it's up.

marika: would appreciate that :thumbsup:

sam: also add a small Kotlin example showing how to safely upload with `RequestBody.create(MediaType, ByteArray)` vs streaming `RequestBody` and doc comments explaining tradeoffs.

marika: will do. closing the thread once PR merged. thanks!
